Legs.Subject: NumberTheoreticTransform.Modulus and the declared odd factor 262111 of Modulus - 1, tested for primality
Legs.Against: Oracles.ExactPrimality — trial division by the primes below 8192 then twenty independent strong-probable-prime rounds, sharing no code and no idea with PrimeField64.IsPrime's twelve-round witness set

Legs.Subject: PrimeField64.IsPrime agrees with the independent oracle on both Modulus and the declared factor 262111, and 262111 * 2^44 + 1 equals Modulus exactly (the claimed factorization is re-derived from the two numbers rather than merely asserted)

PrimitiveRoot's multiplicative order over Modulus, decided by BigInteger.ModPow at the group order and at the order divided by each of the two prime factors (2 and 262111) — the Pocklington-style certificate: a candidate generates the whole group of order c*2^k exactly when it is not one at either (c*2^k)/2 or (c*2^k)/262111
Legs.Against: BigInteger.ModPow, the BCL's own modular exponentiation, sharing no code with PrimeField64.Pow's Montgomery-ring chain (ScaledResidueRing64)

Legs.Subject: Inverse(Forward(x)) == x EXACTLY, bit-for-bit, at lengths 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64, 256 and 1024 over Pcg32XshRr-seeded field elements. Every step is exact field arithmetic (no rounding, no saturation anywhere in PrimeField64), so agreement is a bit-exact identity rather than a measured bound — a fused-substrate leg does not apply because nothing here rounds.

a wrong NttPlan.Length getter breaks this case rather than passing it silently: NumberTheoreticTransform.Forward and Inverse both check the operand span's length against the plan's Length before running, so a Length that answered anything other than the length the plan was built for throws on every call this case makes, which Laws.Claim reports as a failure.

Forward(a) + Forward(b) == Forward(a + b) pointwise EXACTLY, at lengths 1 through 1024, where the addition on both sides is PrimeField64's own field Add — the DFT over a field is linear by the definition of the sum, and nothing here rounds, so the identity holds bit-for-bit rather than within a bound (the fixed-point FFT's linearity sibling, fft.linearity-bound, is the one that needs a bound).
NumberTheoreticTransform.Convolve at lengths 1 through 1024 over Pcg32XshRr-seeded content, with the boundary values zero and Modulus - 1 forced onto the first one or two lanes
Legs.Against: Oracles.CyclicConvolutionModulus — the O(N^2) definition-form sum in BigInteger, reduced once per output rather than diagonalized through a transform at all. The subject runs forward-forward-pointwise-inverse; the oracle never forwards, never inverts and never multiplies pointwise — the two share no algorithm, only the theorem that connects them.

Legs.Subject: the comparison is EXACT equality, not a bound: field arithmetic never rounds, so a correct convolution theorem implementation reproduces the O(N^2) sum bit-for-bit.

every documented refusal, asserted by exception TYPE and by the parameter name it reports: NttPlan.Create at zero, a negative length and a non-power-of-two length (3 and 6) — the largest power of two an int can name is 2^30, far below MaximumLog2Length, so no int length is ever refused for exceeding the prime's own two-adicity ceiling; Forward and Inverse given a span whose length does not equal the plan's; Convolve given a right or destination span of the wrong length; PointwiseMultiply given spans of unequal lengths.
